versions.changelog:
Version 1.1.5 – Major CLI command flow update.

- Replaces direct CLI calls and npx usage with a dedicated script: all commands now run via scripts/run-agent-command.mjs.
- Updates CLI selection guidance: do not use bare calle or npx; never write shell commands as text.
- CLI readiness and authentication flows updated for new entry point and JSON argument format.
- Description updated: new users now receive 100 free credits instead of 20 free calls.
- Removes skill-card.md and adds scripts/run-agent-command.mjs.

No user-facing or functional changes in this version.

- No file changes detected in version 1.1.4.
- No updates to features, documentation, or behavior.

- Product and CLI names updated from "Call-E" to "CALL-E" throughout documentation and metadata.  
- CLI npm package version for npx command updated from @call-e/cli@0.3.0 to @call-e/cli@0.3.2.
- CLI install label changed from "Install Call-E CLI" to "Install CALL-E CLI."
- No logic or file changes; documentation and dependency references only.

- Improved authorization flow: now always use CLI-provided messages and instructions for authentication and do not invent or rewrite URLs or request user credentials.
- Error handling and user prompts updated: clearer instructions if authorization help is missing, guiding users to follow CLI instructions.
- Progress replies for in-progress calls now handle more edge cases; will display more useful fallback messages if activity or status is missing.
- Clarified polling cadence for ongoing calls, ensuring the user receives regular updates every 10 seconds.
- Removed the pre-written authorization template; always rely on CLI for messages.
- No file/code changes; only documentation updates in SKILL.md.

- Updates pinned CLI version in documentation and guidance from @call-e/cli@0.2.1 to @call-e/cli@0.3.0.
- Expands and clarifies the readiness flow for authentication and login, including a new two-step browser-based auth process.
- Adds first and post-authorization message templates for better user guidance.
- Clarifies how to process and display latest call status and progress, specifying exact handling of activity updates and polling intervals.
- Explicitly forbids paraphrasing or free-form commentary on call results; all outputs must use the provided templates and headings.

Version 1.1.0

- Updated skill name and description to clarify functionality and highlight free call credits for new users.
- Expanded supported use cases to include making, running, and checking the status of real outbound phone calls.
- Documentation improvements: streamlined introduction, clarified when to use the skill, and made user guidance more actionable.
- No changes to code or CLI flows. This release focuses on clearer, more user-friendly documentation.

**Call-E skill now uses the calle CLI directly and no longer depends on the OpenClaw plugin.**

- CLI-based workflow: Replaced OpenClaw plugin management with direct usage of the calle CLI for all core actions (setup, auth, planning, call execution, and status).
- New readiness flow: Added explicit CLI help, authentication checks, and tool listing for environment readiness and recovery.
- Updated safety and consent rules: Only place calls when the user intends to; never ask for double confirmation after planning.
- Added step-by-step CLI selection and usage instructions, preferring repo-local or global calle CLI, with npx fallback.
- Reference documentation for command usage is now included in `references/commands.md`.

- Added detailed instructions for plugin setup, feature usage, and safety considerations.
- Clarified when to use (and not use) Call-E for real phone calls, call status checks, scheduling, batch calls, and transcripts.
- Explained step-by-step setup flows: installing, enabling, and verifying the plugin, with fallback installation methods.
- Outlined security, consent, and environment requirements, including handling authentication and agent responsibilities.
- Listed expected command-line tools and summarized agent workflow for planning, running, and checking calls.
- Emphasized clear user intent and provided guidance for handling errors or blocked execution.
